payload.name: Add system-level eval to federated
payload.description:
Complete the unfinished work from the previous session where system-level evaluation in federated mode was identified as "the main missing piece." In the `src/fed_rag/evaluators/federated.py` evaluator, after the existing client-level attack blocks (data poisoning, membership inference, knowledge extraction, node availability), add a new system-level evaluation block that:

1. Builds global knowledge stores that represent "the world after aggregation":
   - `global_clean_store` from all clean client data
   - `global_poisoned_store` from all poisoned client data (when poisoning is enabled)
   - `global_attacked_store` that respects dropped/byzantine clients from node availability attacks

2. Runs the same four attacks against the global stores:
   - System Data Poisoning: measures baseline vs global poisoned BLEU/EM/F1
   - System Membership Inference: tests if query is in the global combined store
   - System Knowledge Extraction: extracts from the global store
   - System Node Availability: builds global store from active clients only, tests query performance

3. Adds new matrix records for each system attack prefixed with "System ...", producing two rows per attack (one client-level, one system-level) in the final evaluation matrix.

This mirrors DRAG's simulator.py behavior where attacking one peer degrades the entire network. The user explicitly said they "don't need to attack on trained fed-rag" — so no FL training/FedAvg rounds are needed. The system-level scope is at the knowledge-store/aggregation level only.

Also ensure the existing tests pass and the output matrix includes both client and system records.

payload.summary: Phase 1 complete. Added a full system-level evaluation block to src/fed_rag/evaluators/federated.py after the existing client-level blocks. The block builds global knowledge stores from combined client data and runs all 4 DRAG-compatible attacks (data poisoning, membership inference, knowledge extraction, node availability) at the system level, producing 4 new matrix records prefixed with 'System ...'. Also fixed a pre-existing bug where node availability evaluations passed the original dataset (lacking client_id) to evaluate_rag_answers, causing dropped_clients/byzantine_clients filtering to have no effect — both client and system node availability blocks now correctly use _flatten(clients). End-to-end evaluator run produced 8 records (4 client + 4 system) with correct degradation metrics. All existing security tests pass.

payload.finalSummary: Completed the unfinished system-level evaluation for FedRAG federated mode. Also fixed a pre-existing bug where node availability evaluations passed the unflattened dataset (lacking client_id) to evaluate_rag_answers, rendering dropped_clients/byzantine_clients filtering ineffective. The evaluator now outputs 8 records total (4 client + 4 system) with correct degradation metrics. All existing security tests pass.
